record.content_text:
Usman and Adamu are at a birthday party. There is a cake that is cut into 4 pieces:

![](https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-06-001.png)

Suppose Usman gets $\frac{1}{4}$ of the cake:

![](https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-06-035.png)

Suppose Adamu also gets $\frac{1}{4}$ of the cake:

![](https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-06-002.png)

If they put their pieces of cake together, they have $\frac{2}{4}$ of the cake:

![](https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-06-003.png)

We write this as:

$$
\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{4}=\frac{2}{4}
$$

record_links.rationale: This note explains the denominator as the number of equal parts when adding fractions.

heading_path.h3: Adding fractions with the same denominator

record.evidence_quote: Remember that the denominator of a fraction tells us into how many parts a whole is divided. In this case, one whole cake is divided into 4 pieces. Together, the boys have 2 of those pieces.

record.content_text:
In Chapter 4, you learnt how to write a fraction in its simplest form. This is when the numerator and denominator have no common factor.

The simplest form of $\frac{2}{4}$ is $\frac{1}{2}$.

![](https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-06-004.png)

We may therefore write:

$$
\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{4}=\frac{1}{2}
$$

record_links.rationale: This worked example adds fractions with different denominators by first finding the LCD.

heading_path.h3: Worked example 6.3: Adding fractions with different denominators

record.answer_text:
Step 1: Compare the denominators. If they are different, find the LCD.

The LCD of 2 and 3 is 6.

Step 2: Find equivalent fractions with the LCD as their denominators.

$$
\frac{2}{3}=\frac{4}{6}
$$

$$
\frac{1}{2}=\frac{3}{6}
$$

Step 3: Use the LCD to represent the parts of one whole in a diagram.

In this case, there must be 6 parts.

Step 4: Shade the number of parts shown by the first numerator of the equivalent fraction.

This is 4.

Step 5: Shade the additional parts shown by the second numerator of the equivalent fraction.

The second numerator is 3. We must shade another 3 parts.

There are only 2 "gaps" in the shape that can be shaded. Therefore, we need to add another shape.

Step 6: Write the total shaded part as a fraction.

The fraction is \frac{7}{6}.

Remember, the denominator shows into how many parts one whole is divided. The numerator shows the total number of those parts that we are dealing with.

Step 7: Write the answer in its simplest form or as a mixed number.

$$
\frac{7}{6}=1\frac{1}{6}
$$

Step 8: Write out the whole calculation.

$$
\begin{array}{l}
 \phantom{00}\frac{2}{3}+\frac{1}{2}\newline
 =\frac{4}{6}+\frac{3}{6}\newline
 =\frac{4+3}{6} \newline
 =\frac{7}{6} \newline
 =1\frac{1}{6}
 \end{array}
$$

heading_path.h3: Exercise 6.2: Add and subtract fractions that have different denominators

record.evidence_quote: ### Exercise 6.2: Add and subtract fractions that have different denominators Calculate each of the following. 5. \frac{1}{8}+\frac{5}{6}+\frac{5}{10}

record_links.rationale: This worked example adds mixed numbers by converting them to improper fractions.

record.answer_text:
Step 1: Convert the mixed numbers to improper fractions.

$$
2\frac{4}{5}=\frac{(2\times5)+4}{5}=\frac{14}{5}
$$

$$
1\frac{2}{3}=\frac{(1\times3)+2}{3}=\frac{5}{3}
$$

Step 2: If the denominators differ, find equivalent fractions with the LCD as their denominators.

The LCD of 3 and 5 is 15.

$$
\frac{14}{5}=\frac{42}{15}
$$

$$
\frac{5}{3}=\frac{25}{15}
$$

Step 3: Write down the LCD and add the numerators of the equivalent fractions.

$$
\begin{array}{l}
 \phantom{00}\frac{42}{15}+\frac{25}{15}\\
 =\frac{42+25}{15} \\
 =\frac{67}{15}
 \end{array}
$$

Step 4: Simplify the answer by converting the improper fraction to a mixed number.

$$
\begin{array}{l}
 \phantom{00}\frac{42}{15}+\frac{25}{15}\\
 =\frac{42+25}{15} \\
 =\frac{67}{15} \\
 =4\frac{7}{15} \\
 \end{array}
$$

record_links.rationale: This item asks learners to add mixed numbers.
